name: orchestrator_read
description: Read one page of a resource the resource parameter lists, such as the ticket list or a ticket. Follow next_offset, and next_resource where a page names one.

resource.description: The resource, one of: tickets: ticket cards, newest first; a card's state is person/review after a ready report, person/blocked or person/failed after those reports, person/answer with a question, person/delivery when an input could not reach the worker, working or working/queued while it works, idle once the worker ended its turn without a report, else how the ticket ended; triggers: trigger cards with where each went, newest first; threads: subscribed threads, newest activity first, with their labels, tickets, current assessment and polling errors; thread/<key>: one thread: its label and link, its tickets and latest decisions, and its triggers, newest first; decisions: decisions, newest first; decision/<id>: one decision with its audit; information: the authoritative information records of cross-role messages, newest first, with their kind, direction, source, target, hops and delivery state (issue #13); information/<id>: one information record whole, including its payload and origin chain; directives: the person's unconsumed Directives, newest first, with the original words, the addressed Session, its project and Ticket, and whether the upward hops were delivered (issues #20–#22); directive/<id>: one Directive whole, including its source, parent hop, effect and when it was consumed; ticket/<id>: a ticket's card, the trigger, decision and threads it is tied to, its latest assignments with the start of each report, and its inputs, newest first; ticket/<id>/assignment: its assignment text; ticket/<id>/assignments: its assignments, newest first, with the start of each report; ticket/<id>/inputs: its inputs, newest first; ticket/<id>/result: its latest report; ticket/<id>/report/<id>: the report of one of its assignments; ticket/<id>/transcript: its Executor Session's messages, newest first; ticket/<id>/message/<n>: one message of that transcript; ticket/<id>/input/<id>: one input it was delivered; trigger/<id>: a trigger's text, where it went, the message it replies to and the messages around it on its thread; settings: settings by block, each with the revision a save names: the small blocks whole, the Policy and the Source instances summarized; settings/proposals: pending settings proposals with per-field diffs, newest first; settings/<block>: one settings block whole, as orchestrator_settings_save takes it: policy, eval, executor, pause or source:<id>; prompts: the prompt revision each Session reads, the skills, and the saved versions; prompts/<revision>: one prompt version by number, or current, the one the Session works under; prompts/defaults: the built-in prompt configuration, and the built-in parts by the key an override names; prompt-preview/<id>: a composed prompt that orchestrator_prompts_save previewed; models: model providers, the DSH default and each role's model; models/<provider>: one provider's models; feishu/<trigger-id>/…: a Feishu original, as the dsh-superagent-further-feishu skill describes; github/…: a GitHub original, as the dsh-superagent-further-github skill describes.

offset.description: Copy next_offset from the previous page; it counts characters of a text and items of a list.

limit.description: Characters of a text, 4000 by default and 8000 at most, or items of a list, 20 by default and 50 at most.

name: orchestrator_route
description: Route candidates, one item each by trigger_id, in one call: accept an explicit request as a new ticket, attach a trigger to an existing ticket, stop a ticket on a person's stop message, or ignore a candidate needing no ticket or stop. Each item is answered alone; a refused item leaves the others. An inferred candidate may only be ignored here.

trigger_id.description: The candidate card's trigger_id; deciding it decides its batch.

title.description: accept: a short label of at most 200 characters describing the original request.

deliverable.description: accept: what the work owes; `answer` is read-only and has no branch or pull request, `review` is a read-only review of a named subject (default change).

review_scope.description: accept with deliverable review: the named subject and standard; required for a review.

repository.description: review: the repository the review reads; omitted, the Ticket's registered project names it.

ref.description: review: the ref (branch, tag or commit) to read; default HEAD.

standard.description: review: the standard or checklist the subject is judged against.

worktree_name.description: accept: Meaningful short English ticket name, e.g. fix-plan-color. Translate Chinese titles into English; no Chinese, pinyin or generic ticket names. 1–4 lowercase words in kebab-case, at most 32 characters.

acknowledgement.description: accept: one brief sentence of at most 100 words naming the concrete change and intended result in the source language. It is posted as a reply to the original source, so do not quote it.

note.description: accept and attach: Optional routing background or explicit human constraint, at most 30 words. Never add implementation instructions or replace the original source.

project.description: accept: the registered Execution project that owns the work, when the Trigger names no repository.

deliverables.description: accept: one entry per delivery unit when the request splits across projects; `after` names earlier indexes it waits on.

reason.description: ignore and stop: why, at most 500 characters; an ignore needs it.

name: orchestrator_lead_instruction
description: Relay a person's instruction about one Ticket to its project Lead, who decides and acts on it. The Orchestrator never commands a worker directly (ADR-0008): this writes a durable instruction for the Lead and prompts it. Actions: attach a Trigger, stop the Ticket, retry a stuck Assignment, pass a note to the worker, or ask the worker that reported waiting for a status report.

trigger_id.description: The Trigger to attach, for action attach.

text.description: The note's text, for action note.

reason.description: Why the person stopped the Ticket, for action stop.

name: orchestrator_trigger_requeue
description: Queue a trigger for a fresh assessment, such as after its Source's access changed; a follow-up that reached a ticket returns only from its worker.

name: orchestrator_eval
description: Load a proactive candidate's window and its thread's tickets; repeated calls reuse them.

name: orchestrator_eval_read
description: Read more of a candidate's context with its trigger_id: a message by message_id, an image by image_id, the root, parent, a thread page by cursor, or a file by path.

trigger_id.description: Original candidate ID returned by orchestrator_eval; every reference is scoped to this trigger.

message_id.description: Only for message: omit for the trigger, or the id of a window message or stub.

cursor.description: Only for thread: omit on the first page, then the next_cursor of the window or the cursor of next_read. Never a thread or message ID.

image_id.description: Only for image: an image id the window or a read lists.

offset.description: Text pagination: copy next_offset; keep the other arguments unchanged. Images use 0.

name: orchestrator_eval_decide
description: Record an assessment's decision after orchestrator_eval with the same trigger_id, as admission describes it.

worktree_name.description: Meaningful short English ticket name, e.g. fix-plan-color. Translate Chinese titles into English; no Chinese, pinyin or generic ticket names. 1–4 lowercase words in kebab-case, at most 32 characters.

deliverable.description: What the accepted work owes: a reviewable change that delivers through a pull request, or a read-only answer that never creates a branch or worktree.

project.description: The registered Execution project that owns the work, when the Trigger names no repository; omit otherwise.

deliverables.description: One entry per delivery unit when the request splits across projects; a unit may belong to any registered project, even one other than the Trigger repository; `after` names earlier indexes.

intent_evidence.description: For acceptance: the quotes that establish the three facts.

acknowledgement.description: For acceptance: one sentence in the source language, posted as a reply to the trigger; omit only when a matched rule asks for silence.

name: orchestrator_reply
description: Send an answer, a ready result, or attention requiring human action, as the replies section says; the gate refuses other purposes. purpose=answer needs the worker's registered answer, or the question an answer ticket started from once its report is ready or the ticket completed. purpose=result needs a ticket in person/review after a ready report, a completed or merged one, or a dropped one whose rule asks for a closing message. IM limit: 100 words.

trigger_id.description: The original human question, for an answer only.

human_action.description: Required for attention: the current attention question.

name: orchestrator_thread_unsubscribe
description: Drop every ticket subscription on a thread; later messages there no longer reach those tickets, and a positive decision can subscribe it again.

thread.description: Thread key, for example github:123 or feishu:<chat>:<root message>

name: orchestrator_settings_save
description: Save tier-A settings on an explicit human request; read revisions with orchestrator_read settings.

source.description: With block source: the Source instance id.

reason.description: The person's words asking for the change.

name: orchestrator_settings_propose
description: Propose a tier-B settings change for the operator to approve in the management panel; read pending ones with orchestrator_read settings/proposals.

reason.description: The person's words asking for the change.

name: orchestrator_policy_sync
description: Refresh one Source's part of the Policy from where that Source keeps it, such as the Feishu users of its sync chat.

name: orchestrator_label
description: Add or remove existing labels on the GitHub Issue or pull request a Trigger names. Never creates labels, changes code, closes work or decides a candidate; use only on an explicit human request to label or triage. A non-GitHub Trigger cannot be labeled.

trigger_id.description: The Trigger naming the Issue or pull request.

remove.description: Labels on the target to remove.

name: orchestrator_send_file
description: Deliver one existing file from a project workspace to a Feishu chat as a bot file message, so people away from this machine can read a design or decision document. Only workspace-relative paths; never edits files. Use only on an explicit human request, or when a Ticket asks for the document to be delivered.

trigger_id.description: The Trigger whose chat receives the file; use instead of chat_id.

chat_id.description: A Feishu chat ID (oc_...) when no Trigger names the chat.

project.description: The registered project whose workspace holds the file.

path.description: Workspace-relative file path; absolute paths and .. are refused.

name: orchestrator_request_create
description: Create one installation-level Request with one Ticket per delivery unit. Use automation (the id from an installation automation delivery marker) for work that delivery asked you to act on; use via discovery when you found a problem in superagent itself here — that finding belongs in a Ticket, not an Issue. Every unit names a registered project. The Request records that provenance as its Mandate and runs without external Channels.

title.description: A short label for the whole Request; the first unit falls back to it as its Ticket title.

instruction.description: The complete work: what to do, where, and how to verify it.

automation.description: The installation automation id from the delivery marker; use instead of via.

via.description: Record that you discovered this yourself; use instead of automation.

project.description: Default registered project for units that omit one.

deliverable.description: What the Tickets owe (default change); answer is read-only.

deliverables.description: One Ticket per unit, in order; after names earlier indexes it waits on.

name: orchestrator_issue_create
description: Raise a finding about superagent itself through the self-evolution Issue outlet, whose target repository is fixed. The Eval self-report gate decides: off records nothing, observe keeps a draft a person approves in Overview, auto files within deduplication and a daily cap. When superagent itself is a registered project here, the tool refuses and the finding belongs in a Request through orchestrator_request_create with via discovery instead. It only creates an Issue, never edits or closes one, and must carry evidence, reproduction and no Feishu content, credentials or private local paths.

title.description: A short, specific title for the finding.

evidence.description: What you observed, with the concrete version, output or file that shows it.

reproduction.description: Steps a person can follow to see the problem.

ticket.description: The Ticket whose worker found it, when a ticket found it.

labels.description: Labels to apply only if the target repository already has them; none by default.

name: orchestrator_incident
description: List, read and act on operational incidents: deterministic records of detectable trouble in the installation, with a bounded read-only diagnosis. Please use list or get first. diagnose asks the read-only diagnostician Session for a root cause and a fix plan within the daily budget; dismiss closes a record with a reason; route creates the follow-up work once, after diagnosis, and only when you confirm it. Never use this tool to fix anything yourself.

status.description: Only incidents in this status; omit or open for the ones still live.

reason.description: Why a person decided the record needs no work.

confirm.description: Must be true: creating a Request hands engineering work to a Lead, and filing an Issue reports a superagent finding.

name: orchestrator_escalations
description: List escalated project requests: work a project Lead escalated to the Orchestrator because it belongs outside its own project. Decide each one with orchestrator_escalation_decide so the Lead receives the mandatory reply.

project.description: Only escalations of this registered project.

status.description: Only escalations in this status; omit for every recent one.

name: orchestrator_escalation_decide
description: Decide one escalated project request with the mandatory reply its Lead requires. On accept, name at least one delivery unit: the work becomes one installation-level Request with one Ticket per unit, recorded under an escalation Mandate. Reject and needs-info record the reply and create no work. The reply is delivered to the project Lead.

decision.description: accept starts the work, reject declines it, needs-info asks the Lead for more.

reply.description: The required non-empty reply, in the language of the request.

deliverables.description: accept: one Ticket per unit, in order; every unit names a registered project.

deliverable.description: What the accepted Tickets owe (default change); answer is read-only.

name: orchestrator_correlate
description: Explicitly mark two or more open Requests as the same need (issue #32). Only a person's or the Orchestrator's explicit decision makes this mark; never infer it from similar titles or text. A Request in the group then reports no result of its own: the group reports one combined result when every Request in it has ended. A Request already in a group joins that group; two different groups cannot merge in one call.

requests.description: Two to ten open Request ids.

note.description: Optional note recorded on the links, in the language of the request.

name: orchestrator_prompts_save
description: Save a complete prompt configuration against baseRevision on an explicit user request, never on quoted content; read it with orchestrator_read prompts.

overrides.description: Text in place of a built-in part, by its key in prompts/defaults; a part not named follows its built-in text.

base.description: Key of the built-in text it was edited from; copy as read, or omit.

baseRevision.description: The revision the configuration edits; required unless preview is set.

preview.description: true saves nothing: it composes both roles' prompts and returns their prompt-preview resources.

name: orchestrator_relays
description: List the cross-project relay requests a project Lead handed to you that are not forwarded yet (issue #14). Each names the project it came from, the project it is for and the original text.

name: orchestrator_relay_forward
description: Forward one pending cross-project relay, by relay_id, to the project it names (issue #14). The target project Lead receives the original text with its source; you cannot edit or redirect it.

project.description: The target project id the relay names.

name: orchestrator_directives
description: List the person's unconsumed Directives (issues #20–#22). Each names the original words, the Session a person addressed, its project and Ticket, and the hops that already carried it to you. Act on it within your own authority; the source node acts on it in its own layer, and you may adjust other projects but not that one while it is unconsumed. A Directive is consumed once, by acting on it, and a redelivery is never a second adjustment.

name: orchestrator_notices
description: List the user-notice requests a project Lead raised that wait for your approval (issue #29). Answer each with orchestrator_notice_decide; a refusal states the reason, which goes back to the Lead.

name: orchestrator_notice_decide
description: Approve or refuse one pending user-notice request from a Lead (issue #29). Approval sends the exact words to the origin Ticket's human channel, or to the alert chat, or as attention; refusal needs the reason and is returned to the Lead. A request is answered once.

reason.description: Required when refuse: why the person is not being notified.

name: memory_write
description: Remember a fact, decision, preference or lesson that a later Session should know without rediscovering it. Store the durable content, not the conversation around it; write the same content twice and one memory is kept.

name: memory_search
description: Find remembered facts, decisions, preferences and lessons by keyword in their text or tags, optionally within one project or ticket. Pinned memories come first, then the newest.

name: memory_forget
description: Remove one remembered item by its id, when it is wrong, obsolete, or must not be carried into later Sessions.
